openness_scale.open: Station-level public presence AND a live feed or machine-readable data
openness_scale.partial: Public presence; data through a national portal, or on request
openness_scale.minimal: Operator-level presence only; little station-specific public material
openness_scale.opaque: No meaningful public presence in a language the general public can reach

meta.schema_note: A facility record describes a place and who operates it. A research project that works at that place is recorded in `programmes`, never as the operator or the nation. Corrected 4 Sep 2026 after Beyond EPICA — an EU project, one of ~20 in the EU Polar Cluster — had been filed as an operator of Little Dome C.

stations.name: Alert
stations.official: Canadian Forces Station Alert / Dr. Neil Trivett GAW Observatory
stations.operator: Environment and Climate Change Canada / DND
stations.setting: Rock — coastal, 817 km from the North Pole
observes: WMO GAW global baseline — CO₂ since 1975
stations.note: The northernmost permanently inhabited place on Earth. Its carbon dioxide record, running since 1975, is the northern anchor of the global network — the curve you have seen from Mauna Loa has a northern twin, and this is where it is measured.

stations.name: CHARS
observes: Northwest Passage sea ice and marine observation
stations.note: Built in a Nunavut community rather than on an empty shore, and explicitly designed to bring Inuit Qaujimajatuqangit — Inuit knowledge — into the research programme rather than treating it as background colour. The Northwest Passage runs past its window and is now navigable in most summers.

stations.name: EastGRIP
stations.operator: Niels Bohr Institute, University of Copenhagen (international consortium)
observes: Deep ice core through an active ice stream
stations.note: The first deep core ever drilled through a moving ice stream. The Northeast Greenland Ice Stream drains about 12 % of the ice sheet and nobody knows why it flows where it does — the ice beneath the camp travels 55 m a year and the borehole moves with it. Bedrock was reached in 2023 at 2,670 m.

stations.name: Ny-Ålesund Research Station
stations.operator: Norwegian Polar Institute / Kings Bay AS
stations.setting: Rock — former mining settlement on a fjord
stations.gateway: Longyearbyen → Ny-Ålesund (Dornier 228)
stations.note: The most internationally shared place in the Arctic: ten nations keep buildings in one former coal settlement of about forty winter residents. Kongsfjorden is the best-observed case anywhere of an Arctic fjord turning Atlantic — the winter sea ice that used to close it now often never forms.

stations.name: Severny Polyus (drifting)
stations.locality: Position drifts with the pack ice
stations.setting: Purpose-built ice-resistant vessel frozen into the pack
stations.note: The Soviet and Russian drifting stations ran from 1937 to 2013, camped directly on the pack. They stopped because the ice stopped being thick enough to camp on. The replacement is a ship built to be frozen in deliberately — an admission, in steel, that the surface those expeditions relied on is gone. Its position is not fixed; the coordinate shown is nominal.

stations.name: Summit Station
stations.locality: Summit of the Greenland ice sheet
stations.setting: Ice sheet — 3,216 m, ice ~3 km thick
observes: Snow accumulation and surface energy balance
stations.gateway: Kangerlussuaq → LC-130 ski-equipped Hercules
stations.note: The highest point of the Greenland ice sheet, and the northern counterpart to South Pole: an atmospheric baseline where the air arrives having touched almost nothing. In July 2012 and again in August 2021 it rained here — the first time rainfall had been recorded at Summit. In 2012, melt reached 97 % of the ice-sheet surface for a few days in July.

stations.name: Utqiaġvik Baseline Observatory
observes: CO₂, CH₄ — one of NOAA's four global baseline observatories
stations.note: One of four NOAA global baseline observatories, and the Arctic one. Its methane record is the most watched in the north because the ground around it is thawing. Utqiaġvik is an Iñupiat community that has hunted bowhead from the ice edge here for more than a thousand years; the shorefast ice that makes that possible now breaks up weeks earlier than it did.

stations.name: Union Glacier Camp
stations.note: The only commercial camp on the continent with a runway that takes wheeled intercontinental aircraft on natural blue ice. Tourists, marathon runners, South Pole skiers and several national programmes all move through it. Chile's Glaciar Unión station shares the site. It is the clearest example of a private operator holding infrastructure that public science now depends on.

observes: Deep ice core targeting 1.2 million years
stations.gateway: Traverse or Twin Otter from Concordia, 35 km

programmes.name: Beyond EPICA – Oldest Ice
programmes.funder: European Commission, with national agencies in ten European countries
programmes.coordinator: CNR-ISP, with Ca' Foscari University of Venice

stations.note: Thirty-five kilometres from Concordia, on the same East Antarctic dome, a drill camp opened for one project: to reach the oldest continuous ice on Earth. In January 2025 the drill reached bedrock at 2,800 m. If the chronology holds, the bottom of that core carries air from before the Mid-Pleistocene Transition — the moment the planet's glacial rhythm changed from 41,000 to 100,000 years, for reasons nobody has established. The camp is Italian and French infrastructure, run by the same two operators as Concordia; Beyond EPICA is the project that uses it, not the body that runs it.

stations.note: A three-kilometre runway on bare blue ice, built by ALCI over two seasons and maintained with the Princess Elisabeth team. The first intercontinental flight landed here on 22 November 2019 — an Ilyushin 76 direct from Cape Town. It is the third wheeled entry point into Dronning Maud Land, after Novo and Troll, and the one that lets Princess Elisabeth be reached without transiting a Russian station.

programmes.funder: European Commission, with national agencies in ten European countries
programmes.coordinator: CNR-ISP, with Ca' Foscari University of Venice

programmes.name: EPICA (European Project for Ice Coring in Antarctica)

stations.note: Jointly run by France and Italy at Dome C, 1,100 km inland and three vertical kilometres up. Winter temperatures fall below −80 °C and no aircraft comes for nine months. The EPICA core taken here holds 800,000 years of atmosphere; its successor project, Beyond EPICA, is drilling at Little Dome C 35 km away for 1.2 million. ESA studies this crew because isolation here is the closest thing on Earth to a long-duration spaceflight.

stations.gateway: Cape Town → Progress → overland traverse (~1,400 km)
stations.note: The coldest temperature ever measured at the surface of the Earth — −89.2 °C, 21 July 1983 — was recorded here. Below the station lies Lake Vostok, 4 km of ice above a body of liquid water the size of Lake Ontario, sealed off for millions of years. The Vostok core was the first to show carbon dioxide and temperature moving together across four glacial cycles.

stations.name: Halley VI
stations.setting: Brunt Ice Shelf — floating ice, ~150 m thick
observes: Ozone (Dobson record from 1956 — the hole was found here)
stations.gateway: Cape Town → Novolazarevskaya (Novo) runway → ski-way
stations.note: The station that found the ozone hole, in 1985, from a record begun in 1956. Halley VI is on skis because the Brunt flows about 400 m a year toward the sea; the buildings have been towed inland twice. Since the Halloween Crack and Chasm 1 began propagating, BAS has not wintered anyone here — the station runs itself through the dark and a summer team returns to it. It is the clearest case on the continent of an instrument outliving its occupants.
